constraints.video.signal_limits.luminanc.evidence: luminance (y) must be between -1% and 103% (-7mv and 721mv)

assets.video.bitrate.mode.evidence: 5.1.1 UHD Video Codec: 'The AVC / H.264 coded video in each MXF file must have a mean data rate (mean value across the entire file) of at least:' followed by a table of per-format floors (200Mb/s .. 500Mb/s)
assets.video.bitrate.mode.note: the doc specifies a minimum MEAN data rate across the whole file, not a fixed rate — that phrasing implies variable bitrate. The word 'variable' itself is not used in the source; derived from how the floor is expressed.

assets.video.color.range[0].evidence: 'Full range video levels must not be used for delivered television programmes.' (§1.2.1), read together with the 10 bit (HD & UHD) row of the signal-range table: Expected Video Range 64–940.
assets.video.color.range[0].note: the doc states full-range is prohibited (a negation), not the literal token 'limited'. Same pattern as clearcast_commercials' assets.video.color.range[0] record, which was also method=model for an equivalent range-by-citation rather than range-by-token statement.

assets.video.quality.colour_bars.mode.matched: §4.1 Programme Layout for File Delivery table: bars/UHD line-up positioned at 09:59:30:00 for a duration of 20", immediately preceding Programme which starts at 10:00:00:00
assets.video.quality.colour_bars.mode.note: same table already cited for the sibling field assets.video.quality.colour_bars.window_s=20; the table's positioning of bars before the programme start is the literal basis for 'required_head'.

assets.audio.track_count.min.evidence: §4.7 Audio Channel Allocations AS-11 DPP X1 table: '1st Track — 2 [channels] — Stereo Main Mix — L, R — Eng — 1' and '2nd Track — 6 [channels] — Surround Main Mix — L,R,C,LFE,Ls,Rs — Eng — 1', with 'the sound tracks listed in the table below must always be included in the MXF file in the order specified'.
assets.audio.track_count.min.note: derived by summing the channel counts of the two MANDATORY sound tracks (2 + 6 = 8) — the doc does not state '8' directly anywhere. Flag for human review: the doc's own vocabulary distinguishes 'Sound Track' (2 mandatory) from 'channel' (8 mandatory channels across those 2 tracks), and this field's exact semantics (tracks vs channels) should be confirmed against how the QC engine counts audio tracks.

constraints.video.signal_limits.rgb.max.note: same table already cited for constraints.video.signal_limits.luminance.min=20 (literal); the table's intro sentence states the Preferred Minimum/Maximum range applies to 'the RGB components and the corresponding Luminance (Y) signal', so 984 covers rgb.max as well as luminance.

constraints.video.pse_standard.evidence: §3.2.3 UHD Programmes: 'HDR test devices must be compliant with ITU-R BT.1702-2 but contact the broadcaster for the latest advice on testing UHD programmes.'
constraints.video.pse_standard.note: the source states BT.1702-2, not BT.1702-3 as currently asserted — needs a human ruling. This is the only ITU-R BT.1702 mention found anywhere across TechnicalDeliveryStandardsBBCFile.pdf, TechnicalDeliveryStandardsBBC.pdf, and AMWA_AS_11_X1.pdf.

constraints.timing.duration.tolerance_ms.evidence: §4.7/4.8: audio-only file 'duration and timecode must exactly match the principal MXF file'; §4.1 layout table requires frame-exact timecode positioning throughout; assets.video.frame_rate.allowed[0]=25 (already cited literal).
constraints.timing.duration.tolerance_ms.note: 40ms = one video frame at the doc's base 25fps rate (1/25s), following the same derivation clearcast_commercials used for the identical field/value. Not itself a number stated in the source — flag for human review, since at the profile's other allowed rate (50fps) the equivalent single-frame tolerance would be 20ms.

structure.type.evidence: §4.1 Programme Layout for File Delivery: a Time-code / Duration / Video / Audio table positioning elements continuously from 09:59:30:00 through Programme start at 10:00:00:00 and beyond.
structure.type.note: the doc does not use the literal word 'timeline' as a structural label (unlike clearcast_commercials, which had a literal section header 'Timeline of a commercial or sponsorship'); inferred here from the continuous timecode-positioned layout table.
